provenance: Original fictional teaching requests. Claims are hypotheses to investigate, not verified findings. These are public design inputs, not hidden tests or answer keys.

requests.question: Our machine got every example right. Has it learned a useful rule?
requests.audience: First-time visitors who can sort shapes but have not studied statistics.
requests.constraints: A short tactile investigation; explain the mechanism without equations.
requests.material: A toy collection with shape, colour and labels. Several copied examples carry different filenames.
requests.proposed_claim: A perfect score on a random split proves the system will work on new collections.
requests.deliverable: A manipulable experiment, a counterexample, an explanation tied to the observed result, and a next question.

requests.question: Why does a useful rule stop working when the collection changes?
requests.audience: Visitors returning from the first exhibit.
requests.constraints: Preserve their previous trial and compare two explicit assumptions.
requests.material: A second synthetic collection changes the relationship between colour and label while keeping the shape convention.
requests.proposed_claim: Changing a colour palette cannot affect a machine's predictions.
requests.deliverable: Choose what to hold fixed, show an input-dependent comparison and distinguish a measured error from its explanation.

requests.question: Does the better overall score mean everyone benefits?
requests.audience: A mixed group comparing two toy classifiers.
requests.constraints: Keyboard-only and no reliance on colour; preserve uncertainty.
requests.material: Two aggregate accuracy figures but no subgroup membership or subgroup error counts.
requests.proposed_claim: The classifier with higher aggregate accuracy has fewer errors in every subgroup.
requests.deliverable: Explain what the supplied evidence can support, identify missing evidence and propose a labelled synthetic counterexample without presenting it as measured data.

revision.change: The curator discovers duplicated items crossing the original evaluation split.
revision.preserve: Earlier notebook results as historical runs; mark affected interpretations for review.
revision.question: How should the inquiry and its explanation change while the original observation remains inspectable?
revision.source_change: The new source packet has citation metadata but no usable full text for one proposed claim. Treat the missing evidence explicitly; a local replay can exercise missing fields without altering the real source.
revision.audience_change: The revised visit has half the initial duration, needs keyboard-only operation and must retain the scientific caveat.
revision.comparison: Apply the earlier source-handling, inquiry-design and exhibit-review approaches to this request first. Preserve the results, improve the weak layer on identical inputs and replay another successful inquiry.

transfer: Create a new inquiry with a different question, source packet and interaction constraint. Reuse the authoring approach, not the previous answer.

source_requests.need: Inspect a bounded set of real bibliographic results, select a relevant stable identifier and resolve its record. Read accessible primary content to support the chosen claim.
Repeat for a different question. Preserve what was actually read separately from titles, abstracts and inaccessible links.
